text:
Maria: Heads-up — we need to finalize our preemptible pool sourcing for Q3. quotas in eu-west are tight and spot churn has spiked. should we move from price-optimized to capacity-optimized bidding for our training pools?

Chad: agree on eu-west congestion. capacity-optimized is safer but costs can jump. do we have historical interruption rates by region for the last 30d?

Priya: I pulled numbers earlier: us-west-2 interruptions ~ 6% last month, eu-west-1 ~ 18%, asia-south ~ 28%. capacity-optimized in eu-west reduces interruptions to ~11% in our small test.

Kevin: Important: interruption rate alone isn't the whole story. We need the cost-per-successful-hour metric. cheaper instances that get preempted waste more setup time.

Maria: yep. proposal: mixed strategy per workload class — "best-effort" (embeddings/batching) = price-optimized with elastic retry; "checkpointed-training" = capacity-optimized with higher bid floor; "low-latency-infer" = reserved/dedicated. Thoughts? :thinking_face: 

Priya: sounds good. for checkpointed jobs add a 15% bid ceiling above on-demand to reduce evictions. example: if on-demand 3.00/hr, cap spot bid at 3.45. that kept us below 12% evict in tests.

Chad: can we automate that ceiling? want rule like: bid = min(on_demand * (1 + ceiling_pct), market_max) and fallback to reserved if predicted runtime > X hours. put it in the autoscaler policy.

Kevin: +1 to automated rule. also add a cooling period to avoid oscillation: if pool sees >10% drains in 10m, temporarily increase reserved fallback ratio by 20%.

Maria: operational workflows: 1) prefer capacity-optimized in congested regions 2) use price-optimized in low-interrupt regions 3) automated bid ceiling = 15% for training, 25% for long-run hyperparam sweeps 4) instant fallback to dedicated if remaining runtime > 2h and eviction risk > 20%.

Priya: how do we detect "remaining runtime"? estimator from job metadata + savepoint frequency. we should expose hint in job spec: `spot_fallback_policy: prefer_dedicated_if_runtime_gt_seconds`.

Chad: good call. also need a k8s node pool naming scheme and priority classes. suggestion: `spot-price-<region>-<gpu-type>` and `spot-capacity-<region>-<gpu-type>` so autoscaler can match by label.

infra-bot: deploy/batch-autoscaler: policy update queued by Maria. review at 12:00 UTC. :wave:

Kevin: one more thing — network limits in eu-west: ephemeral NIC quotas hit during scale-outs. add staged ramp-up: max 10 nodes / 60s per pool. avoids cloud provider throttles.

Maria: agreed. I'll roll a PR with the policy and a config snippet. sample policy block I'll add to the repo:```json
{
  "pools": [
    {"name":"spot-capacity-usw2-v100","strategy":"capacity-optimized","bid_ceiling_pct":15,"ramp_rate_nodes_per_min":20},
    {"name":"spot-price-euw1-a10","strategy":"price-optimized","bid_ceiling_pct":10,"ramp_rate_nodes_per_min":10}
  ],
  "fallback": {"dedicated_ratio":0.2, "dedicated_threshold_seconds":7200}
}
```

Priya: looks sensible. can you include telemetry events: `spot_eviction`, `fallback_trigger`, `avg_setup_seconds` so we can compute wasted compute?

Maria: will add metrics and a Grafana dashboard. I'll schedule the PR review and rollout window. Expecting config rollout next Tue during low traffic.

Chad: reminder: update runbooks for on-call to include quick manual fallback steps and a script to shift jobs to dedicated pools.

Kevin: I'll add quota check job to run every 4h and notify #incidents if projected capacity < 1.2x demand.

Maria: thanks team — seems we have an actionable plan. tagging owners: Chad (autoscaler rules), Priya (telemetry + tests), Kevin (network/quota guards). infra-bot will post follow-ups. :thumbsup:
